item.title: Derivations of the idealization of the incidence module over the finitary incidence algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.24120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a unital commutative ring and $X$ a partially ordered set. Let $FI(X,R)$ and $I(X,R)$ be the finitary incidence algebra and the incidence module of $X$ over $R$, respectively, and let $D(X,R)=FI(X,R)\oplus I(X,R)$ be the idealization of the $FI(X,R)$-bimodule $I(X,R)$. We give a description of the Lie algebra of derivations of $D(X,R)$ and also provide some necessary or sufficient conditions on $R$ and $X$ for the description of this Lie algebra to be simpler.
item.dc:creator: \'Erica Zancanella Fornaroli, Roger Emanuel Moraes Pezzott

item.title: Special identities of nonsymmetric bicommutative operations in associative algebra with an operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.24555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be an associative non-unital algebra with a linear operator $S$ satisfying \[aS(S(b)c)=S(aS(b))c,\] and define $a\prec b=aS(b)$ and $a\succ b=S(a)b$. We determine the special identities of these two operations. If $K_n$ is the arity-$n$ kernel of the corresponding operad morphism and $D_n$ is the space of consequences of smaller-arity kernel elements, then for every $n\geq8$ the quotient $K_n/D_n$ has dimension $n-2$. A basis is given by the classes of $F_{n-2}$, $\rho F_{n-2}$, $G_{n-3}$, $\rho G_{n-3}$, $J_{n-4}$, $\rho J_{n-4}$ and $H_{p,n-p-1}$, $4\leq p\leq n-5$. The upper bound is proved by a direct reduction of singleton sectors, using pure normalization, rigid boundary contraction and the four-singleton corner. The lower bound is obtained from coefficient functionals and a corner projection. In particular, new independent special identities occur in every arity $n\geq8$, and the operadic kernel is not finitely generated.
item.dc:creator: Bauyrzhan Sartayev, Abdibek Ydyrys

item.title: $\frac{1}{2}$ derivations and biderivations of 3-dimensional nilpotent Lie-Yamaguti algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.24852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and their corresponding local and 2-local analogues on three-dimensional nilpotent Lie--Yamaguti algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic zero. Utilizing the established classification of these algebras, we explicitly determine their structures of $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations. Furthermore, we characterize the matrix representations of their local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Our findings demonstrate that, for the non-abelian algebras under consideration, the space of local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations is strictly larger than that of ordinary $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. In addition, we construct examples of 2-local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations that fail to be global $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Finally, a complete characterization of the biderivations for these algebras is provided.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Oubba

item.title: A characterization of generalized derivations and biderivations on some simple algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.24868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we characterize the generalized derivations and biderivations of the simple seven-dimensional anticommutative algebra \(D\) and the seven-dimensional central simple commutative algebra \(C\). Furthermore, we prove that any local generalized derivation of these algebras is inherently a generalized derivation.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Oubba

item.title: Metric preservation under approximate algebraic laws
item.description: arXiv:2610.24927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate which metric information can be retained when an initial metric space is realized in a complete algebra satisfying quantitative laws. Using free metric realizations, we express preservation of designated distances as constraints on the permitted errors. In a fixed weighted-path presentation, the associated feasible error budgets form a closed, convex, upward-closed region with finite-path certificates of failure, and free term distances depend continuously on the budgets. For an idempotent binary operation with positive coordinate weights $a+b=1$, we establish sharp associativity-defect bounds and an exact formula for the generator distances in the free realization with associativity tolerance $\alpha$: $\min\{d_X(x,y),\alpha/(ab)\}$. This yields explicit injectivity and isometry thresholds. We also give a necessary diameter bound when both idempotence and associativity are approximate, and a countably presented example whose free distance is continuous but not Lipschitz at zero.
item.dc:creator: Daksh Pandey

item.title: Rank and Border Rank Additivity of Complex Tensors with a Hankel Summand
item.description: arXiv:2610.24982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the CP rank of a complex Hankel tensor of order $m\ge3$ is additive with that of every complex tensor of the same order. Together with the known equality of CP and symmetric ranks for complex Hankel tensors, this yields symmetric rank additivity whenever the other summand has equal CP and symmetric ranks. We also prove that ordinary and symmetric border ranks coincide and are additive on direct sums of complex Hankel tensors of any common order at least three. Their common value is the sum of the middle binary catalecticant ranks. For order three, we further prove border-rank additivity when the other summand has border rank at most three, or is symmetric with at most five essential variables.
item.dc:creator: Jianze Li

item.title: Classification of Hom--Lie structures on finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.25056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the Hom--Lie structures on finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from \(2\) and \(3\). Except for the three-dimensional simple Lie algebra and the Zassenhaus algebras, every such structure is a scalar multiple of the identity. In the two exceptional cases, we determine the full Hom--Lie space: it has dimension six for the three-dimensional algebra, while for a Zassenhaus algebra it consists precisely of the multiplication operators arising from the corresponding divided-power algebra. This proves a conjecture of Makhlouf and Zusmanovich.
item.dc:creator: Jiacheng Sun, Chi Zhang, Haoran Zhu

item.title: The four-dimensional Sklyanin algebras revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.25541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a theta-function and projective-geometric account of the four-dimensional Sklyanin algebras. We define a family of quadratic algebras by declaring that their relations are precisely the two-tensors vanishing on the graph of a translation automorphism on a quartic complex elliptic curve and the vertex pairs where the vertices are the singular points of the four singular quadrics that contain it. We then use Jacobi's addition formulas for theta functions to produce a set of six explicit relations that coincide with Sklyanin's RLL-relations associated to Baxter's elliptic solutions to the 2 x 2 Yang-Baxter equation. We use the geometric definition to show that these algebras coincide with Feigin and Odesskii's four-dimensional elliptic algebras. Our approach agrees with that of Rains-Ruijsenaars theta function perspective on the four-dimensional Sklyanin agebras. For example, the rank-two secant-line relations of Levasseur-Smith coincide with their two-variable theta function relations. We give explicit theta-function formulas for the degree-two central elements, previously obtained by Levassuer-Smith, that annihilate various families of line modules.
item.dc:creator: S. Paul Smith

item.title: 2-Local Derivations on Conformal Galilei Lie Algebras and Their Central Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify 2-local derivations on the finite-dimensional conformal Galilei Lie algebras in three natural settings: the algebra without central extension, the mass central extension, and the exotic central extension. No additivity or linearity is assumed in the definition of a 2-local derivation. We prove that in every case each 2-local derivation is an ordinary derivation. For the unextended algebra, the proof combines characteristic-quotient normalization with separating vectors, invariant bilinear forms, rank-two mixed zero anchors, and a semisimple-perturbation argument for the standard module. For the mass central extension with $2\ell\ge3$, the residual map is first reduced to the center and then eliminated by a symplectic-anchor construction on the Heisenberg radical; a dimension argument in the centralizer of a regular semisimple element simultaneously handles singular reductive actions and the additional central shear that occurs in spatial dimension two. The endpoint $\ell=\tfrac12$ is the Schr\"odinger algebra; a self-contained symplectic-anchor proof includes all spatial dimensions, with explicit treatment of dimensions one and two. For the exotic extension, after center normalization we use conjugate middle-weight positions and an affine middle anchor to eliminate every central translate, including the one-sided middle-weight configurations. Consequently the set of 2-local derivations coincides with the derivation algebra for all admissible parameters, and hence every 2-local derivation in these families is automatically linear.
item.dc:creator: Bekzod Sultonboyev, Bakhtiyor Yusupov

item.title: Classification of all non-split central extensions of naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.25820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper deals with the naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras over the field of complex numbers. There are two finite series of such algebras, defined in every dimension starting from five, and two further algebras which occur only in dimension five. For each of these algebras we classify, up to isomorphism, all of its non-split central extensions, of every possible dimension. The one-dimensional central extensions are already known from an earlier work, so the main part of the paper is devoted to the extensions of dimension two and higher. As usual, the classification is reduced to the description of the orbits of the automorphism group of the algebra on the subspaces of its second cohomology space with trivial coefficients. For each algebra and each dimension we give the complete list of these orbits together with the multiplication tables of the corresponding algebras, and we point out the extensions whose annihilator coincides with the added central ideal. Among the algebras obtained there are 2-filiform Leibniz algebras which are not naturally graded; this class of algebras has not been systematically studied so far.
item.dc:creator: Kobiljon Abdurasulov, Jobir Adashev

item.title: Dual Reflection Groups from Solutions to the Yang--Baxter Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that $r: X^2 \to X^2$ is a nondegenerate, involutive solution to the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation. To this data, we can associate an Artin--Schelter regular algebra $A$ and an infinite family of groups $G_k$, where $k \geqslant 1$. For each $k$, we show that $G_k$ is a dual reflection group for $A$, in the sense the component of $A$ graded by $1_{G_k}$ is again Artin--Schelter regular. We also show that, using the additional structure afforded by the underlying solution to the Yang--Baxter equation, one can determine the centre, Koszul complex, and associated twisted superpotential for $A$.
item.dc:creator: Simon Crawford

item.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.26060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.
item.dc:creator: Altyngul Naurazbekova, Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.26613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=w\lambda$ for real or octonion $\lambda$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(w\lambda_1)\lambda_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $\lambda_2\lambda_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Grigorian

item.title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[ X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i), \qquad X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t. \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang

item.title: All totally real abelian number fields of class number one are Euclidean
item.description: arXiv:2610.24900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean.
item.dc:creator: Harald Grobner

item.title: Derived equivalence classification of twisted and generalized multifold extensions of affine type
item.description: arXiv:2610.25312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $B$ be a piecewise hereditary algebra of affine type over an algebraically closed field. In this paper we give a derived and stable equivalence classification of twisted multifold extensions of $B$. The types $\widetilde D$ and $\widetilde E$ are already covered by the classification for tree type. We therefore consider the remaining types $\widetilde{A}_{p,q}$. We show that the $n$th power of the Nakayama functor on the full subcategory of a transjective component determines the twist, including its action on morphisms, up to conjugacy in the derived Picard group of a hereditary algebra. Together with the hereditary derived type and the folding number, this gives a complete invariant for derived equivalence, and also for stable triangle equivalence. We then compute these conjugacy classes in the unbalanced, balanced, bypass, and Kronecker cases, keeping the finite rotation data. Finally, by the normalization theorem of Asashiba--Kimura--Nakashima--Yoshiwaki, we obtain the same classification for generalized multifold extensions with nonzero integer jump.
item.dc:creator: Hideto Asashiba

item.title: Superschemes and supermanifolds with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action
item.description: arXiv:2610.25564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that given an analytic supermanifold $X$ over a complete field on which the additive supergroup $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ of super-dimension $0|n$ acts freely (in an appropriate sense), the quotient $X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ exists as an analytic supermanifold, and the canonical morphism $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is an $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. A stronger version of this result is proven for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds, whereby $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is a trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. Previously, Polishchuk [18] established an algebro-geometric analogue, which proves that a superscheme $X$ with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action gives rise to a locally trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-torsor $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$. This result is proven here in an alternative, elementary way. To all of these, a Hopf-algebraic approach is effectively employed.
item.dc:creator: Akira Masuoka, Takuya Oe

item.title: Principal bundles in supersymmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.25811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We discuss rather basic problems on super principal bundles for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds (over $\mathbb{R}$) and analytic supermanifolds over a complete field of arbitrary characteristic. Sharper answers are obtained for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds and for homogeneous supermanifolds. Among others, it is proved for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds that given a $C^{\infty}$-supermanifold $B$ and a super Lie group $G$, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence (up to isomorphism) between the $G$-super principal bundles over $B$ and the $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$-principal bundles over $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$, where $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$ (resp., $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$) denotes the ordinary Lie group (resp., manifold) associated with $G$ (resp., $B$). To prove this, we show a generalized, equivariant version of the renowned Batchelor Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Akira Masuoka

item.title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.26048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Santonastaso, Yue Zhou

item.title: Isotropy Groups of $\sigma$-Derivations on the Quantum Plane
item.description: arXiv:2605.20516v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal A_q=\Bbbk_q[x,y]$ be the quantum plane, with $q\in\Bbbk^\ast\setminus\{1\}$. For a fixed automorphism $\sigma$ of $\mathcal A_q$, we study $\sigma$-derivations and their isotropy groups under the conjugation action of the centralizer of $\sigma$ in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal A_q)$. For $q\neq\pm1$, we use Jordan's classification of skew derivations for toric automorphisms, which generalizes the description of Almulhem and Brzezi\'nski for the quantum plane, to describe these groups by character equations on the torus $(\Bbbk^\ast)^2$, obtaining an arithmetic criterion for finiteness. In this case, we also prove that, for every fixed $\sigma$, every finite subgroup of the torus occurs, up to isomorphism, as the isotropy group of a $\sigma$-derivation, including when $q$ is a root of unity. For $q=-1$, we classify the $\sigma$-derivations for both toric and flip automorphisms $\sigma$ and describe their isotropy groups. In particular, we explicitly determine the isotropy groups of ordinary derivations of $\mathcal A_{-1}$.
item.dc:creator: R. Baltazar, R. Cavalheiro

item.title: On the Regularity and Clean Properties of Matrices over Dual Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2609.29468v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study regularity and clean-type decompositions for matrices over dual numbers. We characterize the von Neumann regularity of dual matrices by establishing a necessary and sufficient compatibility condition between their real and dual components. At the element level, we determine the conditions under which an individual dual matrix $\mathcal{M} = A + B\epsilon$ is regular, $\pi$-regular, nil-clean, or strongly nil-clean. Using the solvability of Sylvester matrix equations, we show that the matrix ring over dual numbers $M_n(\mathbb{D})$ is strongly $\pi$-regular and strongly clean. Moreover, $M_n(\mathbb{D})$ is $\pi$-regular, clean, $r$-clean, strongly $r$-clean, $\mathrm{NR}$-clean, and strongly $\mathrm{NR}$-clean. On the other hand, $M_n(\mathbb{D})$ fails to be regular, strongly regular, nil-clean, strongly nil-clean, and uniquely $\mathrm{NR}$-clean, although it inherits several strong decomposition properties from $M_n(\mathbb{R})$. Our characterizations at the element level show exactly when each property holds.
item.dc:creator: Berrin \c{S}ent\"urk

item.title: Rota-Baxter operators and factorization of Lie affgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.14838v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Rota-Baxter operators on Lie affgebras by an identity independent of the choice of origin and prove that they induce descendant Lie affgebra structures. We establish a bijection between ordered affine Lie factorizations and idempotent operators split at a chosen idempotent fixed point. A cokernel obstruction determines the existence of this point, while invariance under the structural endomorphisms characterizes splitting. We also determine when weighted descendants satisfy the affine Jacobi identity and when operators of nonzero weight give affine doubles. For canonical Lie affgebras, we describe all affine Rota-Baxter operators by Lie subalgebra decompositions and translation vectors, and classify them up to automorphism in dimensions at most two.
item.dc:creator: JiaJia Han, Abror Khudoyberdiyev, Yunzhou Xie, Yi Zhang

item.title: Partial actions of inverse categories and their algebras
item.description: arXiv:2405.13212v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we introduce partial and global actions of inverse categories on posets in two variants, fibred actions and actions by symmetries. We study in detail actions of an inverse category $\mathcal{C}$ on specific subposets of the poset of finite subsets of $\mathcal{C}$, the Bernoulli actions. We show that to each fibred action of an inverse category on a poset there corresponds another inverse category, the semidirect product associated to the action. The Bernoulli actions give rise to the Szendrei expansions of $\mathcal{C}$, which define an endofunctor of the category of inverse categories. We extend the concept of ''enlargement'' from inverse semigroup theory to inverse categories, and we show that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their Cauchy completions are equivalent categories; in particular, some pairs corresponding to partial and global Bernoulli actions are enlargements. We conclude by studying convolution algebras of finite inverse categories and showing that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their convolution algebras are Morita equivalent. Furthermore, using Kan extensions we also analyze the infinite case.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo M. Alves, Willian G. G. Velasco

item.title: Sign-coherence and tropical sign pattern for rank $3$ real cluster-cyclic exchange matrices
item.description: arXiv:2509.07454v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The sign-coherence about $c$-vectors was conjectured by Fomin-Zelevinsky and proved by Gross-Hacking-Keel-Kontsevich for integer skew-symmetrizable case. We prove this conjecture associated with $c$-vectors for rank 3 real cluster-cyclic skew-symmetrizable case. Simultaneously, we establish their self-contained recursion and monotonicity. Then, these $c$-vectors are proved to be roots of certain quadratic equations. Based on these results, we prove that the corresponding exchange graphs of $C$-pattern and $G$-pattern are $3$-regular trees. We also study the structure of tropical signs and equip the dihedral group $\mathrm{D}_6$ with a cluster realization via certain mutations.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Akagi, Zhichao Chen

item.title: Ultrahomogeneity of monounary algebras
item.description: arXiv:2603.26616v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A structure is ultrahomogeneous if every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures can be extended to an automorphism of the structure. The aim of this paper is to provide an explicit description of ultrahomogeneous monounary algebras of arbitrary cardinalities. We also show that a monounary algebra is ultrahomogeneous if and only if it is 1-ultrahomogeneous. These results are then viewed in the context of a several related concepts, including $\omega$-categoricity, homomorphism-homogeneity, (partial-)homogeneity, and transitivity.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Quinn-Gregson

item.title: Hyper-Operations and Coherent Plasmas over $\mathbb{F}_1$
item.description: arXiv:2604.24568v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The additive structure of $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules (in the sense of Segal's $\Gamma$-sets) differs fundamentally from that of abelian groups: addition is encoded through a family of $n$-ary hyper-operations that are multivalued and need not satisfy classical associativity. We establish a \emph{law of generalized associativity} showing that, despite this failure of strict associativity, every $n$-ary sum is contained in the iterated hypersum associated with any partition of its inputs. This enables us to give a hyper-additive description on $\pi_0$ of Schwede's linearization functor $-\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_1} \mathbb{Z}: \mathbb{F}_1\mathbf{Mod} \to \mathbf{Ab}$ that universally strictifies the hyper-additive structure of $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules into classical abelian group addition. We then introduce coherent plasmas, whose algebraic structure encodes the coherence condition inherent in $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules. We construct fully faithful nerves for these structures and their finite-arity truncations, yielding a compatible tower of adjunctions, as well as a coherent Segal condition that characterizes the essential image. The levels of these nerves are represented by powerset plasmas $P_n$, which arise as algebraic realizations of representable $\Gamma$-sets, analogous to standard simplices in geometric realization.
item.dc:creator: Luqiao Xu

item.title: Singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type and standard eventually homological isomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2609.03365v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We refine the definition of eventually homological isomorphisms so that it becomes more natural and fruitful. We introduce singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type which can be viewed as standard singular equivalences of different levels and are more convenient for reducing various homological conjectures and transferring homological properties. We develop the theories of singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type for $n\ge 2$ and standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories by giving their characterizations in terms of $\otimes$-(co)perfect complexes of bimodules, two constructions via opposite algebras and tensor product algebras, examples induced by homomorphisms of algebras and idempotents, and applications to the reduction of homological conjectures such as the finitistic dimension conjecture, Gorenstein symmetry conjecture and Auslander-Reiten conjecture, as well as to the preservation of homological properties such as Gorensteinness, the Fg condition, Happel's property and Han's property. Moreover, we show that essentially surjective standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories correspond to standard singular equivalences with canonical left adjoint.
item.dc:creator: Yang Han, Yongyun Qin, Xianqing Wang
